A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AT-GRPO study despite the title change. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding algorithms, tables, figures, and relocated appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen3 experiments across game, planning, coding, and mathematics, including benchmark results, Plan-Path ablations, and training curves.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, reward and single-agent controls, agent-count scaling, latency measurements, and case studies. Some external baseline scores are explicitly cited rather than newly produced.

M1.justification: v3 replaces the stated log-probability loss with a clipped importance-ratio objective and specifies intra-turn state updates (Sec. 3, Algorithm 1). Appendix B revises code/tester reward definitions, broadcasts math/Sudoku terminal rewards across turns, and changes local reward weights relative to v1 Appendix A.1. These substantially revise the reported procedure; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E1.justification: The original four domains and their datasets remain. v3 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning evaluation in Sec. 5.3, extending coverage within an existing domain.

E2.justification: v3 adds MAS+GRPO to Tables 1–2, multi-turn single-agent variants to Tables 7–8, and numerical comparisons with MAPoRL, MARFT, and CURE in Table 3. The external baseline scores in Table 3 are marked as cited results, not reported reruns.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include multi-turn single-agent controls, ensembles of 2, 3, 5, and 7 agents with a Judge, and comparisons using Phi-3-mini and Qwen2.5 backbones. Appendix G adds a separate four-H100 latency protocol. The original Qwen3 training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original isolation/role-swapping ablation and training curves are retained. v3 adds dense-versus-outcome-only reward ablations, single-agent self-revision controls, agent-count scaling, computational-cost profiling, and game/code failure-and-success case studies (Fig. 5 and Appendices E–H).

E5.justification: The same training curves retain across-run variability bands in v1 Fig. 5 and v3 Fig. 6. v3 introduces no explicit repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its added comparisons.

E6.justification: Retained values in Tables 1–2 and the original Plan-Path ablation are unchanged. v3 adds comparator, scaling, latency, and control results; Table 6 reports 89.0% Plan-Path accuracy with outcome-only rewards versus 93.0% with dense rewards. Table 6 also swaps the Sudoku/Sokoban SA and MAS baseline values relative to Table 2.

T1.justification: v3 adds a verifier-monotonicity assumption, maximizer lemma, and greedy-optimality proposition with proofs in Appendix B.7, plus computational-complexity derivations in Appendix G. Neither analysis appears in v1. The new maximizer lemma is not guaranteed by its stated assumption when verifier rewards tie but Q-values differ.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the central AT-GRPO and multi-policy training claims, role-specialization findings, and headline performance figures. The added evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations for naive MAS+GRPO failures, ineffective single-agent self-revision, independence from dense reward heuristics, and latency savings through earlier termination. It also removes v1's explicit limitations concerning exclusively cooperative tasks and text-only environments from Sec. 6.

D1.justification: v3 adds asynchronous vLLM batching and latency-profiling hardware, batch-size, and timing details. Original training hyperparameters and most prompts remain. It removes v1's explicit code/environment repository link and omits the previous mathematical Tool-agent local-reward specification; repository unavailability itself is not established.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands comparisons with prior MAS training frameworks through MARFT/MARTI discussion and Appendix A's capability matrix. It also explicitly positions agent/turn grouping as an extension of GiGPO and adds supporting references for self-revision, GSM8K, and the theoretical discussion.

P1.justification: The title changes from Stronger Together to Stronger-MAS, Sections 2 and 5.1 are locally rewritten, and existing appendix material is reorganized into Appendices B–D alongside new sections. Most original prose and prompt templates remain, limiting the extent of language and structural revision.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Fig. 3, adds scaling Fig. 5, Tables 3 and 5–8, and case-study boxes, and expands Tables 1–2 with comparator rows. The original ablation table and training figure are relocated to Table 4 and Fig. 6, respectively, with their results retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important gaps in v1 through a direct MAS+GRPO comparison and controls for reward shaping and extra turns. However, its new optimality proof does not follow from Assumption 1 when rewards tie, Table 6 misassigns Sudoku/Sokoban baseline values, and explicit applicability limitations disappear. These empirical benefits and new reliability problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
